# Async and Lifecycle Awareness

When tasks involve concurrent work or long-lived helpers, predictable lifecycle beats maximal throughput.

## Bounds

Cap concurrency to resources you can justify; queue overflow should be defined, not accidental.

## Shutdown

Stop accepting new units, cancel or drain in-flight units with cleanup, then exit. Ensure queued-but-unstarted units have defined semantics.

## Signals

Register termination handling before heavy work starts; exit codes should reflect real outcomes.

## Testing stance

Exercise cancellation and shutdown paths when the task touches them—silent failure during teardown is still failure.
